This Day, The Court Made The Following:
 Order

Petitioner has sought for initiation of appropriate proceedings against respondents 1 to 5 for taking illegal possession of the petition schedule property and has also sought for issuance of writ of mandamus against respondents 1 to 6 not to utilize the petition schedule property for road widening purpose without the acquisition process as per the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Petitioner has also sought for issuance of writ of mandamus to direct respondents 1 to 6 not to block access to the petition schedule property by constructing retaining wall in front of the petition schedule property.

2. Petitioner submits that they are the owner of property morefully described in the schedule and that respondents 4 and 5 have encroached upon their property and accordingly, present petition has been filed.

Sri. Gowthamdev C. Ullal, learned counsel appearing for respondents 4 and 5 submits that the lapse that has occurred as is extracted in the affidavit below, is at the end of the contractor and he has been instructed property.

Learned counsel has filed an affidavit of the Deputy Chief Engineer /
Construction-4, South-Western Railway, Millers Road, Bangalore 560046.

Relevant paragraphs of the said affidavit are reproduced herein below:
"3. I submit
that, the land of the petitioner's is necessary for building a approach road for a proposed road over bridge in the northern side of the petitioner's property.
The said road is proposed for the public purpose.
The respondent nos.1 to 3 have to procure the land for the said purpose.
4. In this regard initial construction material was procured through the contractors of the respondent no.4 and 5 for construction of the road over bridge.

The materials for the said road over bridge was in advertently and by oversight dumped in the petitioner's land under the bonafide NC: 2023:KHC:25421 belief that the said land belongs to the Government since, it was adjacent to the public road.
The contractors without noticing the ownership had also put up a temporary shed for the labours working in the project.
When the dispute was raised by the petitioner a joint survey was conducted in the presence of the petitioner and respondents no. 1 to 5.
During the joint survey it was realize that the place where the construction materials were dumped belongs to the petitioner.

sentences.text: It is submitted that, after realizing the mistake this respondents no.4 and 5 had orally instructed the contractors to commence vacating the property of the petitioner.
In the meanwhile the petitioner had approached this Hon'ble Court.
6. This respondents submits unconditional apology to the inconvenience caused to the petitioner.

The dumping of materials and construction of temporary shed for labour used for project is due to bonafide error in judgment by the contractor, We R4 and R5 undertake to vacate the property within 1 week from today.
7. It is submitted that, the portions of the land is necessary for construction of proposed approach road over bridge.
However, all acquisition NC: 2023:KHC:25421 proceedings will be conducted after following due process of law by this respondents through the appropriate authorities.
This respondent undertakes that they will not enter into forceful possession without following due process of law and procedures contemplated by law will be follow.

Wherefore, it is submitted that the undertaking statements made by this respondents may be taken on record and the above writ petition may be closed against these respondents by taking this affidavit on record."
4. The expressed undertaking of respondents 4 and 5 would make it clear that (a) they would vacate the property within one week from today and (b) if they require the property, they would take recourse to acquisition proceedings.
5. In light of the above, the grievance of the petitioner stands substantially addressed and the matter does not call for any adjudication.

Insofar as the damages that the petitioner may have suffered due to the acts of occupation of the petitioner's property, the said aspect is a NC: 2023:KHC:25421 matter to be taken note of and to be factored in the compensation, in the event the respondents were to take steps for acquisition.
This is in light of the legal right of the petitioner to claim damages for occupation prior to issuance of notification for acquisition.
Nevertheless, if the petitioner feels that there are damages to be claimed, such contention is kept open to be addressed at an appropriate point of time.
6. The respondents are to take appropriate steps to avoid such lapses in future.
7. Accordingly, petition is disposed off.
